title: Dedication: right faith in one Lord; not two sons; Word took ensouled body of Mary Theotokos
english: So I approach and dedicate this discourse to you, most pious empresses. I have composed it concerning the right and blameless faith that is ours toward our Lord Jesus Christ. It especially befits you who are so holy and beloved of God to bind on, together with the highest boasts of the empire, the crown of love toward Christ.

That crown is already fitted to your renowned heads, and the God of all brightens you with unending glories. Yet so that you may shine still more — holding in mind the accurate and unadulterated knowledge of the mystery concerning Christ — I have put together this little treatise, showing through every thought that just as there is one God the Father, from whom are all things, so also there is one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things; and with them, of course, the Holy Spirit.

And having learned to think rightly, we will not put up with those who divide the one Christ and Son and Lord into two sons. For we do not say that the Son begotten before every age from the essence of God the Father is one, and that the one who in the last times came to be from a woman, came to be under the law, is another — but one and the same, both before the true coming-together and union with flesh and still after it.

For the Son from God the Father by nature, taking to himself an ensouled and intelligent body, has been begotten according to the flesh through the holy virgin and Theotokos Mary — not turned into flesh (far from it!), but rather taking it on, and not neglecting to be God.
notes_covered: One Christ; Theotokos; kenosis without change.

title: Philippians kenosis: same one God and human; unchanged Word; economy needs human lowliness
english: For even so he has remained Master of all. These things we have been taught by the saints.

Their words convey wise commands to us: we must hunt what most seems to belong to the holy writings, and scrutinize the truth in the divine doctrines, applying a fine mind to what is said about Christ, tearing down reasonings and every height raised against the knowledge of God, and taking every thought captive to his obedience.

For it is firmly held and confessed by all that the Word from him by nature, existing in the form and equality of God the Father, “did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a slave, coming to be in the likeness of humans; and being found in fashion as a human he humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even death on a cross.”

So the mind that aims to discern well the force of what is written about him must somehow be filled with God-loving skill — so that the same one may be recognized as God and human together, and may have his being God without falsification. For the Word’s nature is unchangeable, and he does not refuse the measure of the emptying: the one who economically endured voluntary emptying for us does not blush at his own designs.

He must therefore be seen as distinguished in the dignities of the deity, and yet not wholly freed from our smallness because of the human — for the economy demands this. For if the Word, being God, has become flesh — that is, human…

title: Joel flesh; human sayings do not disturb; Christ Jesus means Word incarnate; 1 Cor headship
english: …according to “I will pour out from my Spirit upon all flesh.” Let no one be disturbed even if God-breathed Scripture says something about him that befits a human; rather survey his above-world glory, from power and superiority that is God-befitting and highest.

What is most likely to weaken the mind of the simpler, I will try — as far as possible and as well as can be — to make clear, setting beside each saying the solution that suffices for explanation, God again directing our path into this. For he gives “a word to those who proclaim with much power,” as the inspired singer says.

In the discourse we made toward the holy virgins I set out at great length the readier sayings that have nothing hard to grasp; in the present work I have recalled the less clear. For your God-loving majesty needed to know both — these and those — so that through both what is sound for knowledge might settle, like a light, in your most pure minds. My aim in interpreting each is to be brief as I can; and the discourse on the emptying has been set first of all.
Know this nonetheless: whenever Christ Jesus is named to us, it befits us to understand the Word from God the Father as having become human and been enfleshed.

“For I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, the head of a woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God. The first human is of the earth, dusty” — that is, Adam — “the second is from heaven” — clearly Christ. But “just as we wore the image of the dusty,

title: Christ second Adam our head; Father head of the Word; he became poor being rich
english: let us also wear the image of the heavenly,” as it is written. So the first head of our race — that is, beginning — was the one of earth and dust. But since Christ has been named second Adam, he has been set as head — that is, beginning — of those being remolded through him toward him into incorruption by sanctification in the Spirit.

So he is our beginning — that is, our head — insofar as he has appeared as human; yet as God by nature he himself has as head the Father in the heavens, for the Word, being God, has been begotten from him by nature. That “head” signifies “beginning” confirms, for minds that doubt, that the man became head of the woman: for she was taken from him.
So there is one Christ and Son and Lord, who as God by nature has the Father in the heavens as head, and who has become head for us because of kinship according to the flesh.

“For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, for our sake he became poor, so that you by his poverty might become rich.” See clearly here both the superiority of the divine and unmixed nature and the lowliness of the measures of humanity — and besides these the agreement of both into unity, the Only-begotten having lowered himself into this.

For no word could interpret the riches of the deity, while humanity is exceedingly poor, or rather all that it has is God-given and from above — and before all, even being itself: for it was called by God into existence, not existing before. But the rich…
